volume_estimate_after_dedup: By sub-topic in OpenAlex: (a) 240; (b) 323; (c) 1,025; (d) 934; (e) 108 formula/shift-share + 119 citation-chasing + 29 GAEZ keywords = 256. The single-string union for (a)-(d) is 2,416 (sum of parts 2,522, so about 106 overlap), and (a)-(e) together come to about 2,670 gross. The (e) arms overlap little with (a)-(d), so expect about 2,600 OpenAlex records. Preprint/SSRN/NBER/journal duplicates are common: CGS alone has 3 records and MacKinnon-Webb RI has 4, and 627 of the union records are dated 2026. Version deduplication should bring this to roughly 2,100-2,400 unique works for title/abstract screening, plus about 100-200 new items from the arXiv top-k lists and a few dozen grey-literature records. Main trade-off: (c) and (d) carry about 80% of the volume. Using primary_topic.id:T10845 for (d) would cut it from 934 to 483 while keeping SDID, at the cost of synthetic-control methods papers filed under economics topics. Dropping the subfield filter for (c) and (d) would push the total above 10,000, which is not screenable.
issues_and_limits: Tool limits: the Firecrawl scrape route to OpenAlex is limited to about 10-11 requests per minute, and failed calls also count. About 13 calls failed this way and were re-run. WebFetch to api.openalex.org failed (DNS ENOTFOUND) and Parallel web_fetch returned 429, so OpenAlex was reached only through Firecrawl.

The subfield filter (primary_topic.subfield.id 2002|2613|2000|1804) depends on OpenAlex's automatic topic classifier. It keeps every (a)-(d) seed, but it would drop methods papers filed in health, political-science or agricultural subfields. DRS, Reynier-Rubin and Costinot et al. sit in 1110 or 1105, which is why (e) is left unfiltered or uses citation chasing.

Some key papers lack the obvious terms in their OpenAlex abstracts. CGM 2008 has no 'wild'. AKM 2019 has no 'instrument'. Borusyak-Hull 2023 has no 'shift-share', 'identification' or 'inference'. DRS 2023 and Bustos et al. 2016 have no suitability or GAEZ vocabulary. Because the suitability-as-instrument literature (e) is described in body text, it is poorly retrievable by title/abstract keywords. An optional fulltext.search filter exists in OpenAlex but was not tested.

Year metadata differs between OpenAlex and the published journal issues. Conley-Taber is 2010 in OpenAlex but REStat 93(1), 2011. Ferman-Pinto is 2018 in OpenAlex but REStat 101(3):452-467, 2019. Any date filter must allow for this.

'Few control clusters' (the Ceará case: 15 municipalities with zero dose) is rarely written that way. Adding "few control", "few untreated" and "small number of control" added only 6 records. That literature is mostly indexed under 'few treated' or 'small number of clusters/groups', and the reviewers should check symmetry claims (e.g. Ferman-Pinto, MacKinnon-Webb on unbalanced clusters) during screening.
The single word 'instrument' is noisy (policy instrument, measuring instrument), and so are 'agro-ecological zones' and 'land suitability' (agronomy). These terms were removed or restricted.
arXiv-only preprints can be missing from OpenAlex (e.g. 2507.20415). This is why the arXiv research-index framings are kept as a supplement.
The research index and Scholar Gateway return ranked results without total counts, so their volumes are top-k cut-offs chosen by the searcher, not exhaustive counts.

syntax_findings: OpenAlex title_and_abstract.search accepts uppercase AND/OR, parentheses and quoted phrases. Counts confirm it: A alone 107,552 and B alone 184,104, but A AND B gives 609. The response's x_query.oqo shows the parsed tree.

Nested OR-of-AND groups work in one filter value, e.g. ((X AND Y) OR (Z AND W)), and are parsed into join trees. A single call can therefore return the union of all sub-topic strings, as at orders 73 and 85.

Search is stemmed by default ('stemmed' in the oql). A quoted phrase also matches inflected forms, and unquoted single words are stemmed individually. Hyphens are equivalent to spaces: "difference-in-differences" and "difference in differences" both return 74,518.

Comma-separated filters are ANDed and pipes give OR within one filter field (e.g. primary_topic.subfield.id:2002|2613|2000|1804; cites:W1|W2). OR across different filter fields, such as subfield OR topic, is not possible in one call.
Known-item recall works by adding doi:A|B|C as a separate filter. The 10.48550/arxiv.* DOIs resolve, and the SDID arXiv DOI 10.48550/arxiv.1812.09970 resolves to the merged AER record.
authorships.author.display_name.search is invalid (HTTP 400). Use raw_author_name.search for author-name search.

primary_topic.id:T10845 ('Advanced Causal Inference Techniques') holds most of the methods seeds. topics.id:T10845 (any of a work's topics) is broader and suited the shift-share arm. CGM 2008 is primary T11911 and AKM is T14051, which shows the topic-filter risk.
cites:<W-ids> combined with a title_and_abstract.search vocabulary filter gives a screenable, reproducible citation-chasing arm (1,709 down to 119).
group_by returns only per-page groups: per-page=1 showed just the top group, so set per-page to the number of groups needed.
